question: The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).
reference_sql: SELECT b.class_symbol_id, m.name AS method_name FROM code.class_bases b JOIN code.symbols c ON c.symbol_id = b.class_symbol_id JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = c.file_id JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname = c.qualname || '.' || m.name WHERE b.base_symbol_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py::SQLDatabase' AND NOT f.is_test AND m.is_public AND m.name NOT IN (SELECT bm.name FROM code.symbols bm WHERE bm.file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py' AND bm.kind = 'method' AND bm.qualname LIKE 'SQLDatabase.%') ORDER BY 1, 2
source_check: Checked connectors/base.py: SQLDatabase defines __init__, execute, get_tables, get_columns, get_queries, get_views, get_pks, get_fks, dialect, database_name, qualify, close, __enter__, __exit__ (no ping, no get_schemas). grep 'def ping' finds exactly one in each of clickhouse, databricks, heavydb, kyuubi, mysql, postgres, snowflake, trino (not duckdb/sqlite). databricks.py has @property auth_mode (l.237), @contextmanager reuse_connection (l.246), get_schemas (l.473), ping (l.985). The 10 production subclasses each name SQLDatabase as their first base. The test subclass connectors/tests/test_base.py::_Fake is excluded. Extractor matched source.

question: Which functions or methods in the click library (src/click/) reach term_len (src/click/_compat.py) within at most two direct calls: either calling it directly, or directly calling a repository function or method that itself calls term_len directly? Give the symbol ID and the minimum number of calls in the chain (1 for a direct caller, 2 otherwise).
reference_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT DISTINCT caller_symbol_id, callee_symbol_id FROM code.calls WHERE call_kind = 'direct' AND callee_symbol_id IS NOT NULL), d1 AS (SELECT caller_symbol_id AS s FROM e WHERE callee_symbol_id = 'src/click/_compat.py::term_len'), d2 AS (SELECT e.caller_symbol_id AS s FROM e JOIN d1 ON e.callee_symbol_id = d1.s) SELECT s AS symbol_id, MIN(h) AS hops FROM (SELECT s, 1 AS h FROM d1 UNION ALL SELECT s, 2 FROM d2) x WHERE s LIKE 'src/click/%' AND s <> 'src/click/_compat.py::term_len' GROUP BY s ORDER BY 1
source_check: Direct term_len callers confirmed by grep: ProgressBar.render_progress (_termui_impl 268, 282), TextWrapper._wrap_chunks (_textwrap 89-154), measure_table (formatting 19), wrap_text (93, 95, in its own body not the nested _flush_par), HelpFormatter.write_usage (180-195) and write_dl (255-256). Second-hop callers: ProgressBar.__enter__/__iter__/generator/update/render_finish call self.render_progress() (lines 117-380); HelpFormatter.write_text calls wrap_text (219). Source has further callers through non-self objects (core.py 1194 formatter.write_usage, 1335/1348/2036 formatter.write_dl in Command.format_usage, format_options, format_arguments and Group.format_commands); the extractor leaves these as dynamic_attribute, and the question's counting rule excludes them. Matches source under the stated rule.

question: Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? question: Within httpx/_client.py, which functions or methods eventually lead to a call of `Client._send_single_request`, through a chain of one or more direct calls whose every step is inside httpx/_client.py? Count direct calls only (no callbacks) and exclude `_send_single_request` itself. Give their symbol IDs.
reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(symbol_id) AS (SELECT caller_symbol_id FROM code.calls WHERE callee_symbol_id = 'httpx/_client.py::Client._send_single_request' AND call_kind = 'direct' AND caller_symbol_id LIKE 'httpx/_client.py::%' UNION SELECT c.caller_symbol_id FROM code.calls c JOIN up ON c.callee_symbol_id = up.symbol_id WHERE c.call_kind = 'direct' AND c.caller_symbol_id LIKE 'httpx/_client.py::%') SELECT symbol_id FROM up WHERE symbol_id <> 'httpx/_client.py::Client._send_single_request' ORDER BY symbol_id
source_check: Followed the chain in httpx/_client.py: _send_handling_redirects calls self._send_single_request; _send_handling_auth calls self._send_handling_redirects (line ~944); send calls self._send_handling_auth; request and stream call self.send; get/options/head/post/put/patch/delete call self.request. AsyncClient's methods call only async counterparts, BaseClient never calls these. 12 symbols, matches the database. Outside the file the chain does continue in source (httpx/_api.py::request does 'client.request(...)' on a Client instance) but the extractor classifies that as a dynamic_attribute call, which is why the question is scoped to httpx/_client.py.
